mal:area.name: MC
mal:area.comment: This specification contains the Monitor and Control area.

mal:service.name: Action
mal:service.comment: The action service allows consumers to request execution of actions and to subsequently monitor the execution progress of these actions via the monitorExecution PUB-SUB operation. A consumer requests execution by calling the executeAction operation. The provider validates the request, creates and archives the ExecutionRequest object, assigns it a unique executionId, and returns that id in the response. The provider then reports execution progress by publishing monitorExecution notifications and storing ExecutionStatus COM objects in the archive. Once the action execution details have been checked and execution started, the executeAction operation completes whilst the execution of the action possibly continues (depends on the actual action). The action service defines three types of objects: ActionDefinition (holds the name, description, and argument list of an action), ExecutionRequest (holds the argument values submitted for a specific execution), and ExecutionStatus (holds the progress status of each stage of an execution).
mal:service.mal:documentation:
The action service shall provide:
  1. the capability for monitoring the execution progress of actions;
  2. the capability for submitting actions for execution;
  3. the capability for listing the numeric identifiers for the action definitions.
The list of actions supported by the action service shall be declared when deploying that service.
The definitions of the actions shall be represented as ActionDefinition COM objects.
Executions of an action that are submitted to a provider using the executeAction operation shall be represented as ExecutionRequest COM object.
The ExecutionRequest object shall use the related link to indicate which ActionDefinition object it uses.
ActionDefinition objects should be stored in the COM archive.
The service provider shall create an ExecutionStatus object for each execution stage reached. Note: it is implementation-specific when a progress step is reached.
ExecutionStatus objects shall be stored in the COM archive.
The ExecutionStatus object shall use the related link to point to the ExecutionRequest it belongs to.
The fields of the ExecutionStatus object shall match the corresponding fields published in the monitorExecution notification for the same stage.

mal:pubsubIP.name: monitorExecution
mal:pubsubIP.comment: The monitorExecution operation allows a consumer to subscribe for updates on the execution progress of actions.
mal:pubsubIP.mal:documentation: When an execution stage of an action is reached, the service provider shall publish an execution progress update.
The service provider shall publish the execution progress update using subscription keys corresponding to the definitionId, executionId, and actionCategory of the executing action.
The PUBLISH message shall include the stageType field in the message body.
A service consumer may subscribe to updates for a specific action definition, or for all action definitions by using the wildcard value in the definitionId field.
A service consumer may subscribe to updates for a specific action execution, or for all action executions by using the wildcard value in the executionId field.
A service consumer may subscribe to updates for a specific action category, or for all categories by using the wildcard value in the actionCategory field.
If the execution stage did not complete successfully, then the success field of the PUBLISH message shall be set to FALSE.
The stageType field shall be set to START when the action begins execution, to PROGRESS for each intermediate progress stage, and to END when the action completes execution.
If the stageType field is START or END, then the step field shall be NULL.
If the stageType field is PROGRESS, then the step field shall be set to the current progress step number.

mal:field.name: definitionId
mal:field.comment: The id of the action definition being executed.

mal:field.name: executionId
mal:field.comment: The id of the ExecutionRequest being executed.

mal:field.name: actionCategory
mal:field.comment: The category of the action.

mal:field.name: stageType
mal:field.comment: The lifecycle stage of the execution update.

mal:field.name: success
mal:field.comment: Indicates whether the execution stage completed successfully.

mal:field.name: step
mal:field.comment: The progress step number within the action execution. Null for START and END stages.

mal:field.name: comment
mal:field.comment: An optional comment providing additional details about the execution stage.

mal:requestIP.name: executeAction
mal:requestIP.comment: The executeAction operation allows a consumer to request execution of an action on the provider. The execution of the action is asynchronous and therefore the executeAction operation may return before the action execution has been completed.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: A service provider may apply deployment-specific checks to the action execution and shall return an INVALID error if they fail.
If an error is raised, then no action shall be executed.
The service provider shall assign an executionId once the action has been accepted for execution but before execution starts.
The RESPONSE message shall contain the assigned executionId.

mal:field.name: executionRequest
mal:field.comment: The argument values and related information of the action to be executed.

mal:field.name: executionId
mal:field.comment: The assigned id of the execution of an action. Used as the executionId subscription key in monitorExecution notifications.

mal:errorRef.comment: When the argumentValues list size does not match the argument list in the matched ActionDefinition, or the argumentIds list does not match the ActionDefinition argument identifiers, or one or more argument values do not match the declared attribute type, or a deployment-specific check fails.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:errorRef.comment: When the definitionId in the executionRequest field does not match a known ActionDefinition object.

mal:requestIP.name: listDefinition
mal:requestIP.comment: The listDefinition operation allows a consumer to request the ids of the ActionDefinition objects for the supported actions of the provider.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The actionNames field may contain the wildcard value of '*' to return all supported ActionDefinition objects.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied identifiers shall be made.
The returned list shall maintain the same order as the submitted list unless the wildcard value was included in the request.

mal:field.name: actionNames
mal:field.comment: The list of action names to retrieve the ActionDefinition ids for.

mal:field.name: ids
mal:field.comment: The list of ids matching the ActionDefinitions.

mal:errorRef.comment: When a supplied identifier does not include a wildcard and does not match an existing ActionDefinition object.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

com:objects.comment: Action definitions, execution requests, and execution statuses are represented as COM objects.

com:archiveUsage.comment: Action definition, execution request, and execution status objects are stored in the COM archive.

mal:service.name: Parameter
mal:service.comment:
The parameter service allows the user to subscribe to parameter value report and optionally be able to set new values. A single PUBSUB operation is provided for monitoring and publishing of parameter values. A parameter value also contains a calculation of the validity of the parameter, the flow chart for this calculation is provided in Figure 3-3: validity calculation flow chart
This standard supports the concept of non-standard invalidity states but the meaning and calculation of these is outside the scope of this standard. The generation of value reports can be controlled using the enableGeneration operation. The parameter service does not include any value checking, this is delegated to the check service. Parameter definitions are maintained using the operations defined in this service but storage of definitions is delegated to the COM archive.
mal:service.mal:documentation:
The parameter service shall provide:
  1. the capability for periodic reporting of predefined parameter values;
  2. the capability for setting the raw parameter value of a set of parameters;
  3. the capability for requesting the current value of a set of parameters;
  4. the capability for controlling reporting of the parameter values;
  5. the capability for maintaining the list of parameter definitions.

Each parameter value report shall contain:
  1. The validity of the parameter value;
  2. The raw value of the parameter;
  3. The converted value of the parameter, if applicable.
The validity of a parameter shall be calculated against the validity criteria in the ParameterDefinition.
The generation of reports for a parameter shall be controlled by the generationEnabled field in the ParameterDefinition.
If the generationEnabled field is TRUE, then the service provider shall generate reports for that parameter.
If the parameter requires periodic reports, then the interval between reports shall be controlled by the reportInterval field in the ParameterDefinition.
If the reportInterval field is set to '0', then no periodic reports shall be generated; reports shall be triggered by another implementation-specific mechanism in this case.

If the parameter is periodic and reported via a periodic aggregation, and a new report has not been received in the aggregation period, then the service provider shall set the validityState field of the ParameterValue to EXPIRED.
If the parameter raw value cannot be obtained, or calculated for synthetic parameters, then the service provider shall set the validityState field to INVALID_RAW and the rawValue field to NULL.

If the validityExpression field is NULL or evaluates to TRUE, and the ParameterDefinition either does not contain a conversion or the conversion is successful, then the service provider shall set the validityState field to VALID.
If the validityExpression field is NULL or evaluates to TRUE, and the conversion of the parameter value fails, then the service provider shall set the validityState field to INVALID_CONVERSION.
If the validityExpression field is not NULL and the parameters used to determine the expression are not VALID, then the service provider shall set the validityState field to UNVERIFIED.
If the validityExpression field is not NULL and the validity expression evaluates to FALSE, then the service provider shall set the validityState field to INVALID.
If the validityState field is INVALID_CONVERSION, then the convertedValue field of the ParameterValue shall be NULL.
If the validityState field is UNVERIFIED or INVALID and the ParameterDefinition contains a conversion, then the convertedValue field of the ParameterValue shall contain the converted value.
Deployment-specific validityState values shall use values greater than 127. Note: the meaning of such values is deployment-specific and outside the scope of this standard.
The definitions of the parameters shall be represented as ParameterDefinition COM objects.
Parameter value reports shall be represented as ParameterValue COM objects.
The ParameterValue object shall use the related link to indicate which ParameterDefinition object it uses.
The source link of the ParameterValue object should be the object that caused the report to be generated.
The source link of the ParameterValue object shall be NULL for periodic reports.
ParameterDefinition objects should be stored in the COM archive.
When a parameter value report is published, the ParameterValue object should be stored in the COM archive.

mal:pubsubIP.name: monitorValue
mal:pubsubIP.comment: The monitorValue operation allows a consumer to subscribe for parameter value reports.
mal:pubsubIP.mal:documentation: The timestamp of the ParameterValue report shall be the time of the parameter value update, taken from the PUBLISH message.
If no source link is needed, then the objId field shall be NULL.

mal:field.name: name
mal:field.comment: The name of the parameter.

mal:field.name: parameterId
mal:field.comment: The id of the ParameterDefinition object.

mal:field.name: parameterValueId
mal:field.comment: The id of the ParameterValue object.

mal:field.name: objKey
mal:field.comment: The ObjectKey of the source link of the report.

mal:field.name: newValue
mal:field.comment: The ParameterValue object value.

mal:requestIP.name: getValue
mal:requestIP.comment: The getValue operation returns the latest received value for a requested parameter.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The wildcard value of '0' shall be supported and matches all parameters of the provider.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied ids shall be made.
If a parameter is being reported periodically, then calling this operation shall not reset the reportInterval timer.
The retrieved value shall not be published via the monitorValue operation.

mal:field.name: paramInstIds
mal:field.comment: The list of ParameterDefinition ids.

mal:field.name: paramValDetails
mal:field.comment: The list of returned ParameterDefinition ids and matching parameter values.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the requested parameters is unknown.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:submitIP.name: setValue
mal:submitIP.comment: The setValue operation allows a consumer to set the raw value for one or more parameters.
mal:submitIP.mal:documentation: If an error is raised, then no modifications shall be made as a result of this operation call.

The service provider shall set all parameter values atomically, such that all values are applied at the same time without interleaving with other set operations. Note: how this is implemented is an implementation detail.
The service provider shall create new ParameterValue objects for the updated parameters, store them in the COM archive, and publish the new values.

mal:field.name: newRawValues
mal:field.comment: The list of ParameterRawValues containing the ParameterDefinition id and the respective raw value to be set.

mal:errorRef.comment: When the paramInstId field contains the wildcard value '0', or one or more of the referenced ParameterDefinitions is unknown.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the referenced parameters is read only.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:errorRef.comment: When the supplied raw value does not match the defined attribute type for the referenced ParameterDefinition.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:requestIP.name: enableGeneration
mal:requestIP.comment: The enableGeneration operation allows a consumer to control whether reports for specific parameters are generated or not.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The ids field shall support the wildcard value of '0', which matches all ParameterDefinition objects of the provider.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied ids shall be made.
If the enable field is TRUE, then the service provider shall generate reports for matching ParameterDefinition objects.
If the enable field is FALSE, then the service provider shall not generate reports for matching ParameterDefinition objects.
The service provider shall not raise an error if the supplied Boolean value is the same as the current generationEnabled field for a matched ParameterDefinition object.
If an error is raised, then no modifications shall be made as a result of this operation call.
If the generationEnabled field is changed, then the service provider shall create and store a new ParameterDefinition object in the COM archive.
If a new ParameterDefinition object is created, then that new object shall become the current ParameterDefinition for the parameter.
If the generation of reports is being enabled and the parameter is defined as periodic, then the service provider shall generate a report immediately and start the report interval from that report.

mal:field.name: enable
mal:field.comment: TRUE to enable report generation, FALSE to disable it.

mal:field.name: ids
mal:field.comment: The list of ParameterDefinition object instance identifiers to enable or disable.

mal:field.name: newObjInstIds
mal:field.comment: The list of ids for the new ParameterDefinition objects.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the requested ParameterDefinition objects is unknown.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:requestIP.name: listDefinition
mal:requestIP.comment: The listDefinition operation allows a consumer to request the ids of the ParameterDefinition objects for the supported parameters of the provider.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The paramNames field may contain the wildcard value of '*' to return all supported ParameterDefinition objects.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied identifiers shall be made.
The returned list shall maintain the same order as the submitted list unless the wildcard value was included in the request.

mal:field.name: paramNames
mal:field.comment: The list of parameter names to retrieve the ParameterDefinition ids for.

mal:field.name: ids
mal:field.comment: The list of ids matching the ParameterDefinitions.

mal:errorRef.comment: When a supplied identifier does not include a wildcard and does not match an existing ParameterDefinition object.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:submitIP.name: updateDefinition
mal:submitIP.comment: The updateDefinition operation allows a consumer to update a definition for one or more parameters. The replacement definition should be stored in the COM archive by the service provider. The operation does not remove the previous object from the COM archive, merely removes the object from the provider.
mal:submitIP.mal:documentation: If an error is raised, then no definitions shall be updated as a result of this operation call.
The service provider shall create a new ParameterDefinition object and store it in the COM archive.
The new ParameterDefinition object shall become the current ParameterDefinition for the parameter.

mal:field.name: paramInstIds
mal:field.comment: The ids of the ParameterDefinition objects to be updated.

mal:field.name: definitions
mal:field.comment: The updated ParameterDefinition objects.

mal:errorRef.comment: When the paramInstIds list contains NULL or '0', or the paramInstIds and definitions lists are not the same length, or a supplied reportInterval value is not supported by the provider.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one of the supplied ParameterDefinition ids is unknown.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

com:objects.comment: Parameter definitions and value instances are represented as COM objects.

com:sourceObject.comment: The object that caused the value to be generated or NULL for periodic reports

com:archiveUsage.comment: Parameter objects and value instance objects are stored in the COM archive.

mal:service.name: Alert
mal:service.comment: The alert service defines the structures and patterns for the publishing and monitoring of alerts. The alert service uses COM event service to monitor and publish alert events. The generation of alerts can be controlled using the enableGeneration operation. Alert definitions are maintained using the operations defined in this service but storage of definitions is delegated to the COM archive.
mal:service.mal:documentation:
The alert service shall provide:
  1. the capability for reporting of alerts;
  2. the capability for controlling reporting of alerts;
  3. the capability for maintaining the list of alert definitions.
The generation of alerts shall be controlled by the generationEnabled field in the AlertDefinition.
If the generationEnabled field is TRUE, then the service provider shall generate instances of that alert.
Alert instances shall be published as events using the COM event operations.
The definitions of the alerts shall be represented as AlertDefinition COM objects.
Instances of an alert shall be represented as an AlertEvent COM event.
The AlertEvent object shall use the related link to indicate which AlertDefinition object it uses.
When an alert is generated it shall be represented as a COM event.
The event shall be published using the COM event service.
The source link of the AlertEvent object shall be the object that caused the event to be generated.
AlertDefinition objects should be stored in the COM archive.
When an alert event is published, the AlertEvent object should be stored in the COM archive by the publisher.

mal:requestIP.name: enableGeneration
mal:requestIP.comment: The enableGeneration operation allows a consumer to control whether updates for specific alerts are generated or not.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The ids field shall support the wildcard value of '0', which matches all AlertDefinition objects of the provider.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied ids shall be made.
If the enable field is TRUE, then the service provider shall generate instances of matching AlertDefinition objects.
If the enable field is FALSE, then the service provider shall not generate instances of matching AlertDefinition objects.
The service provider shall not raise an error if the supplied Boolean value is the same as the current generationEnabled field for a matched AlertDefinition object.
If an error is raised, then no modifications shall be made as a result of this operation call.
If the generationEnabled field is changed, then the service provider shall create and store a new AlertDefinition object in the COM archive.
If a new AlertDefinition object is created, then that new object shall become the current AlertDefinition for the alert.

mal:field.name: enable
mal:field.comment: TRUE to enable alert generation, FALSE to disable it.

mal:field.name: ids
mal:field.comment: The list of AlertDefinition object instance identifiers to enable or disable.

mal:field.name: newObjInstIds
mal:field.comment: The list of ids for the new AlertDefinition objects.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the requested AlertDefinition objects is unknown.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:requestIP.name: listDefinition
mal:requestIP.comment: The listDefinition operation allows a consumer to request the ids of the AlertDefinition objects for the supported alerts of the provider.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The alertNames field may contain the wildcard value of '*' to return all supported AlertDefinition objects.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied identifiers shall be made.
The returned list shall maintain the same order as the submitted list unless the wildcard value was included in the request.

mal:field.name: alertNames
mal:field.comment: The list of alert names to retrieve the AlertDefinition ids for.

mal:field.name: ids
mal:field.comment: The list of ids matching the AlertDefinitions.

mal:errorRef.comment: When a supplied identifier does not include a wildcard and does not match an existing AlertDefinition object.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:submitIP.name: updateDefinition
mal:submitIP.comment: The updateDefinition operation allows a consumer to update a definition for one or more alerts. The replacement definition should be stored in the COM archive by the service provider. The operation does not remove the previous object from the COM archive, merely removes the object from the provider.
mal:submitIP.mal:documentation: If an error is raised, then no definitions shall be updated as a result of this operation call.
The service provider shall create a new AlertDefinition object and store it in the COM archive.
The new AlertDefinition object shall become the current AlertDefinition for the alert.

mal:field.name: definitionIds
mal:field.comment: The ids of the AlertDefinition objects to be updated.

mal:field.name: alertDefDetails
mal:field.comment: The replacement AlertDefinition objects.

mal:errorRef.comment: When the definitionIds list contains NULL or '0', or the definitionIds and alertDefDetails lists are not the same length, or one of the supplied AlertDefinition objects contains an invalid value.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one of the supplied AlertDefinition ids is unknown.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

com:objects.comment: Alert definitions and instances are represented as COM objects.

com:events.comment: AlertEvent objects are published when an enabled alert is generated.

com:event.name: AlertEvent
com:event.comment: The AlertEvent shall be raised when an enabled alert is published.

com:sourceObject.comment: The object that caused the event to be generated

com:archiveUsage.comment: Alert objects and AlertEvent objects are stored in the COM archive.

mal:service.name: Aggregation
mal:service.comment:
The aggregation service allows the user to acquire several parameter values in a single request. Aggregations are generated either periodically, on an ad-hoc basis, or after a configurable timeout when being filtered. Periodic is where they are generated at a specific generation interval; in this case the periodicity is an aspect of the aggregation rather than the contained parameters. Ad-hoc is when the aggregation generation is triggered by some other deployment-specific mechanism. Filtering is where an aggregation is only generated when the change in the value of the filtered parameters exceeds a specified threshold or a timeout is passed. Filtering can be applied to both periodic and ad-hoc aggregations. As there may be a large amount of time between reports of an aggregation when filtering is applied, the filtering concept also has a maximum reporting interval. If a report of the aggregation has not passed the filter in the maximum reporting interval a report is generated regardless. This allows there to be regular reports of an aggregation sent regardless of filtering. It should be noted that applying a filter with a maximum reporting interval to an ad-hoc aggregation will cause the aggregation to generate reports in a periodic way if the maximum reporting interval is left to expire. This is expected behaviour. There are a number of intervals defined in the structures of the service, the diagram in Figure 3-12 illustrates the use of these: insert timing diagram The diagram shows a single report of an aggregation being generated which contains two parameter sets. Each set of parameter values in the aggregation report contains two optional durations, delta time and interval time.
  • The timestamp of the first value of the first set (T1) is defined as the timestamp of the aggregation report plus the delta time of the first set.
  • The timestamp of the second value of the first set (T2) is defined as the timestamp of the first parameter (T1) plus the interval time of the set.
  • The timestamp of the first value of the second set (T3) is defined as the timestamp of the last value of the previous set (T2) plus the delta time of the second set.
  • The timestamp of the second value of the second set (T4) is defined as the timestamp of the first parameter (T3) plus the interval time of the set.
The COM archive is used to hold the definitions of the aggregations.
mal:service.mal:documentation:
The aggregation service shall provide:
  1. the capability for periodic reporting of predefined aggregation values;
  2. the capability for requesting the current value of a set of aggregations;
  3. the capability for controlling reporting of the aggregation values;
  4. the capability for maintaining the list of aggregation definitions.

Three modes of generating an aggregation value shall exist: periodic, ad-hoc, and filtered:
  1. Periodic reports for aggregations shall be generated once for each cycle of a specified interval.
  2. Ad-hoc reports for aggregations shall be triggered by some other deployment-specific means.
  3. Filtered reports for aggregations shall be generated only when the value of one or more parameters in the aggregation has changed by more than a given threshold since the previous generation or when a timeout expires.
The generation of reports for an aggregation shall be controlled by the generationEnabled field in the AggregationDefinition.
If an aggregation is required to send periodic reports, then the interval between reports shall be controlled by the reportInterval field in the AggregationDefinition.
If the reportInterval field is set to '0', then no periodic reports shall be generated; reports shall be triggered by another ad-hoc implementation-specific mechanism in this case.
Periodic aggregation reports shall set the generationMode field of the AggregationValue to PERIODIC.
Ad-hoc aggregation reports shall set the generationMode field of the AggregationValue to ADHOC.
The filtering of reports for an aggregation shall be controlled by the filterEnabled field in the AggregationDefinition.

If filtering is enabled, then the service provider shall generate reports only when the value of one or more filtered parameters has changed by more than the defined threshold since the previous report.
The filter threshold shall be defined on a per-parameter basis, either as a percentage or an absolute delta change in value.
Parameters in an aggregation that do not have a filter specified in the aggregation definition shall be ignored by the filter comparison process.

If filtering is enabled and a filteredTimeout has been set, and no change has been detected within that timeout period, then the service provider shall generate an aggregation value with a generationMode of FILTERED_TIMEOUT.

If the sendUnchanged field in the AggregationDefinition is FALSE, then parameter values that have not changed since the previous report shall be replaced by NULL in the values list of the AggregationSetValue.
The ordering of values in the AggregationValue shall match the ordering of parameters in the AggregationDefinition.
The definitions of the aggregations shall be represented as AggregationDefinition COM objects.
Aggregation value reports shall be represented as AggregationValueInstance COM objects.
The AggregationValueInstance object shall use the related link to indicate which AggregationDefinition object it uses.
The source link of the AggregationValueInstance object should be the object that caused the report to be generated.
The source link of the AggregationValueInstance object shall be NULL for periodic reports.
AggregationDefinition objects should be stored in the COM archive.
When an aggregation value report is published, the AggregationValueInstance object should be stored in the COM archive.

mal:pubsubIP.name: monitorValue
mal:pubsubIP.comment: The monitorValue operation allows a consumer to subscribe for aggregation value reports.
mal:pubsubIP.mal:documentation: The timestamp of the AggregationValueInstance report shall be taken from the PUBLISH message.
If no source link is needed, then the objId field shall be NULL.

mal:field.name: aggregationName
mal:field.comment: The name of the aggregation.

mal:field.name: definitionId
mal:field.comment: The id of the AggregationDefinition object.

mal:field.name: aValObjId
mal:field.comment: The id of the AggregationValueInstance object.

mal:field.name: objKey
mal:field.comment: The ObjectKey of the source link of the report.

mal:field.name: newValue
mal:field.comment: The AggregationValue.

mal:requestIP.name: getValue
mal:requestIP.comment: The getValue operation returns the latest received value for a requested aggregation.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The definitionIds field shall support the wildcard value of '0', which matches all aggregations of the provider.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied ids shall be made.
The service provider shall not apply filtering when responding to this operation.
If an aggregation is being reported periodically, then calling this operation shall not reset the reportInterval or filteredTimeout timer.
The retrieved value shall not be published via the monitorValue operation.

mal:field.name: definitionIds
mal:field.comment: The list of AggregationDefinition ids.

mal:field.name: aggValDetails
mal:field.comment: The list of returned AggregationDefinition ids and matching AggregationValues.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the requested aggregations is unknown.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:requestIP.name: enableGeneration
mal:requestIP.comment: The enableGeneration operation allows a consumer to control whether reports for specific aggregations are generated or not. This affects all types of aggregations, periodic, filtered and ad-hoc.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The ids field shall support the wildcard value of '0', which matches all AggregationDefinition objects of the provider.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied ids shall be made.
If the enable field is TRUE, then the service provider shall generate reports for matching AggregationDefinition objects.
If the enable field is FALSE, then the service provider shall not generate reports for matching AggregationDefinition objects.
The service provider shall not raise an error if the supplied Boolean value is the same as the current generationEnabled field of the matched AggregationDefinition object.
If an error is raised, then no modifications shall be made as a result of this operation call.
If the generationEnabled field is changed, then the provider shall create and store a new AggregationDefinition object in the COM archive.
If a new AggregationDefinition object is created, then that new object shall be the current AggregationDefinition used for the aggregation.
If generation is being enabled and the aggregation is periodic, then the provider shall generate a report immediately and start the report interval from that report.

mal:field.name: enable
mal:field.comment: TRUE to enable report generation, FALSE to disable it.

mal:field.name: ids
mal:field.comment: The list of AggregationDefinition object instance identifiers to enable or disable.

mal:field.name: newObjInstIds
mal:field.comment: The list of ids for the new AggregationDefinition objects.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the requested AggregationDefinition objects is unknown.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:submitIP.name: enableFilter
mal:submitIP.comment: The enableFilter operation allows a consumer to control whether reports for specific aggregations are filtered or not. This affects both periodic and ad-hoc aggregations.
mal:submitIP.mal:documentation: The ids field shall support the wildcard value of '0', which matches all AggregationDefinition objects of the provider.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied ids shall be made.
If the enable field is TRUE, then the service provider shall filter reports for matching AggregationDefinition objects.
If the enable field is FALSE, then the service provider shall not filter reports for matching AggregationDefinition objects.
The service provider shall not raise an error if the supplied Boolean value is the same as the current filterEnabled field of the matched AggregationDefinition object.
If an error is raised, then no modifications shall be made as a result of this operation call.
If the filterEnabled field is changed, then the provider shall create and store a new AggregationDefinition object in the COM archive.
If a new AggregationDefinition object is created, then that new object shall be the current AggregationDefinition used for the aggregation.

mal:field.name: enable
mal:field.comment: TRUE to enable report filtering, FALSE to disable it.

mal:field.name: ids
mal:field.comment: The list of AggregationDefinition object instance identifiers to enable or disable.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the requested AggregationDefinition objects is unknown.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:requestIP.name: listDefinition
mal:requestIP.comment: The listDefinition operation allows a consumer to request the ids of the AggregationDefinition objects for the supported aggregations of the provider.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The aggregationNames field may contain the wildcard value of '*' to return all supported AggregationDefinition objects.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied identifiers shall be made.
The returned list shall maintain the same order as the submitted list unless the wildcard value was included in the request.

mal:field.name: aggregationNames
mal:field.comment: The list of aggregation names to retrieve the AggregationDefinition ids for.

mal:field.name: ids
mal:field.comment: The list of ids matching the AggregationDefinitions.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one of the supplied identifiers does not match an existing AggregationDefinition object.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:requestIP.name: addAggregation
mal:requestIP.comment: The addAggregation operation allows a consumer to define one or more aggregations that do not currently exist. The new AggregationDefinition objects are expected to be stored in the COM archive by the provider of the aggregation service.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: If an error is raised, then no new definitions shall be added as a result of this operation call.
The provider shall create a new AggregationDefinition object and store it in the COM archive.
The returned list shall maintain the same order as the submitted definitions.

mal:field.name: aggDefDetails
mal:field.comment: The name and the AggregationDefinition to be added.

mal:field.name: newIds
mal:field.comment: The list of ids for the new AggregationDefinition objects.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the supplied aggregation names is already in use in the domain.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the supplied aggregation objects contains an invalid name or a supplied interval is not supported by the provider.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:submitIP.name: updateDefinition
mal:submitIP.comment: The updateDefinition operation allows a consumer to update a definition for one or more aggregations. The replacement definition should be stored in the COM archive by the service provider. The operation does not remove the previous object from the COM archive, merely removes the object from the provider.
mal:submitIP.mal:documentation: If an error is raised, then no definitions shall be updated as a result of this operation call.
The provider shall create a new AggregationDefinition object and store it in the COM archive.
The new AggregationDefinition object shall be the current AggregationDefinition used for the aggregation.

mal:field.name: definitionIds
mal:field.comment: The ids of the AggregationDefinition objects to be updated.

mal:field.name: aggDefDetails
mal:field.comment: The replacement AggregationDefinition objects.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the supplied AggregationDefinition ids does not match an existing object.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:errorRef.comment: When the definitionIds list contains a NULL or '0', the two supplied lists are not the same size, or a supplied interval is not supported by the provider.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

mal:submitIP.name: removeAggregation
mal:submitIP.comment: The removeAggregation operation allows a consumer to remove one or more aggregations from the list of aggregations supported by the aggregation provider. The operation does not remove the AggregationDefinition objects from the COM archive, merely removes the objects from the provider. This permits existing AggregationValueInstance objects to continue to reference the correct AggregationDefinition object in the COM archive.
mal:submitIP.mal:documentation: The definitionIds field shall support the wildcard value of '0', which matches all aggregations of the provider.
The service provider shall check for the wildcard value first; if found, no other checks of supplied ids shall be made.
Matched AggregationDefinition objects shall not be removed from the COM archive, only from the list of AggregationDefinition objects in the provider.
If an error is raised, then no aggregations shall be removed as a result of this operation call.
If the operation succeeds, then the provider shall not publish aggregation values for the removed AggregationDefinition objects.

mal:field.name: definitionIds
mal:field.comment: The ids of the AggregationDefinition objects to be removed.

mal:errorRef.comment: When one or more of the supplied AggregationDefinition ids does not match an existing object.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list.

com:objects.comment: Aggregation definitions and value instances are represented as COM objects.

com:sourceObject.comment: The object that caused the value to be generated or NULL for periodic reports

com:archiveUsage.comment: Aggregation definition and value instance objects are stored in the COM archive.

mal:service.name: Conversion
mal:service.comment: The conversion service provides a set of basic conversion definition types that allows the specification of a conversion between two representations. These conversions are used by the other MC services (such as Action, Alert, and Parameter) to define conversions from raw field representations to some engineering representation. Conversions are associated with other entities such as parameters or action/alert arguments through the configuration of the relevant service (action/alert/parameter). The conversion service does not provide any operations directly, but allows consumers to add, remove, and modify conversion definitions via the COM archive.
mal:service.mal:documentation: The conversion service shall provide the capability for maintaining the list of conversion definitions.
The conversion service shall use the COM archive operations for maintaining the conversion definitions.
Updating a conversion definition shall be performed by adding a new conversion definition and referencing it in the service-specific COM objects (such as ParameterDefinition).
A DiscreteConversion shall contain at least one pair of values in the mapping.
A LineConversion shall contain at least two line points.
A PolyConversion shall contain at least one pair of values in the points list.
A RangeConversion shall contain at least one pair of values in the points list.
The definitions of the conversions shall be represented as either DiscreteConversion, LineConversion, PolyConversion, or RangeConversion COM objects.
Each instance of a conversion definition shall be represented by an object instance in the COM archive.
Other service objects shall reference instances of a conversion using the id of the conversion definition.
The COM archive service operations shall be used to add, update, and remove conversions.

com:objects.comment: Conversion definitions are represented as COM objects.

com:archiveUsage.comment: Conversion definition objects are stored in the COM archive.

mal:enumeration.name: Severity
mal:enumeration.comment: The possible severity values for an alert or check. The numerical value represents the increasing severity; therefore CRITICAL is more severe than ALARM. Normally, for checks, only the WARNING and CRITICAL ranges are used: the colour yellow is associated with WARNING, and the colour red is associated with CRITICAL.

mal:item.comment: Indicates a nominal situation with no consequences.
Indicates unexpected behaviour without directly threatening consequences.
Indicates behaviour of serious concern requiring the attention of an operator, but not necessarily a malfunction.
Indicates that the monitored item has malfunctioned. Requires operator attention.
Indicates behaviour with mission threatening consequences. Requires operator attention.

mal:composite.name: ArgumentDefinition
mal:composite.comment: The definition of an argument, including associated attributes such as conversion. The conditionalConversions define the conditions under which a referenced conversion is applied. Only the first TRUE conversion should be applied.

mal:field.name: argId
mal:field.comment: The argument definition identifier.

mal:field.name: description
mal:field.comment: An optional argument description.

mal:field.name: rawType
mal:field.comment: The attribute raw type of the argument.

mal:field.name: rawUnit
mal:field.comment: The unit for the raw value.

mal:composite.name: AttributeValue
mal:composite.comment: A wrapper for an Attribute value. Allows a list of heterogeneous Attribute types to be constructed, unlike a typed List which requires all values to be of the same type.

mal:field.name: value
mal:field.comment: The argument value. Shall not be NULL. NULL may be represented by having a NULL in place of the complete AttributeValue composite.

mal:composite.name: ConditionalConversion
mal:composite.comment: A condition expression paired with a Conversion. The conversion is applied when the condition evaluates to TRUE, or unconditionally when the condition field is NULL.

mal:field.name: condition
mal:field.comment: The expression indicates which entities are applicable for this check. If NULL, then the condition shall evaluate to TRUE.

mal:field.name: conversionId
mal:field.comment: The id of the Conversion to be used if the condition evaluates to TRUE or is NULL.

mal:composite.name: ParameterExpression
mal:composite.comment: A simple Boolean expression comparing a parameter value against a fixed value using an operator.

mal:field.name: parameterId
mal:field.comment: The id of the Parameter to be used in the expression.

mal:field.name: operator
mal:field.comment: The expression operator.

mal:field.name: useConverted
mal:field.comment: If set to TRUE the converted value field of the parameter value should be used, otherwise the raw value field should be used.

mal:field.name: value
mal:field.comment: The value to be used in the expression.

mal:enumeration.name: ActionCategory
mal:enumeration.comment: Contains the default Action category values. It is implementation specific what the meaning of the values are in a particular context.

mal:item.comment: Default category.
Category for high priority actions.
Category for critical actions.

mal:enumeration.name: ExecutionStageType
mal:enumeration.comment: Identifies the lifecycle stage of an action execution update published via the monitorExecution operation.

mal:item.comment: Indicates the beginning of action execution.
Indicates an intermediate progress update during action execution.
Indicates the end of action execution, whether successful or not.

mal:composite.name: ActionDefinition
mal:composite.comment: The definition of an action, including its name, description, category, and argument list.

mal:field.name: name
mal:field.comment: The name of the action. Shall not be empty or the wildcard value.

mal:field.name: description
mal:field.comment: The description of the action.

mal:field.name: category
mal:field.comment: The category of the action.

mal:field.name: progressStepCount
mal:field.comment: Total number of steps that will be reported if PROGRESS reporting is selected in the sent Action. 0 if PROGRESS reporting is not used.

mal:field.name: arguments
mal:field.comment: The list of argument definitions. If no arguments are defined, then the complete list is replaced with a NULL.

mal:composite.name: ExecutionRequest
mal:composite.comment: The information required to execute an action, including the definition identifier and the argument values to use.

mal:field.name: definitionId
mal:field.comment: The id of the ActionDefinition to be used.

mal:field.name: argumentValues
mal:field.comment: List containing the values of the arguments. The ordering of the list matches that of the definition. If a value for a particular entry is not being supplied, then its position is filled with a NULL value. If no arguments are defined, then the complete list is replaced with a NULL.

mal:field.name: argumentIds
mal:field.comment: Optional list of argument definition identifiers. Allows the provider to verify that the correct arguments are being supplied. The ordering of the list matches that of the argument list of the action definition.

mal:composite.name: ExecutionStatus
mal:composite.comment: The progress status of a single execution stage of an action. An ExecutionStatus object is stored in the COM archive each time a monitorExecution notification is published.

mal:field.name: stageType
mal:field.comment: The lifecycle stage of the execution.

mal:field.name: success
mal:field.comment: Indicates whether the execution stage completed successfully.

mal:field.name: step
mal:field.comment: The progress step number. Null for START and END stages.

mal:field.name: comment
mal:field.comment: An optional comment providing additional details about the execution stage.

mal:enumeration.name: ValidityState
mal:enumeration.comment: The validity states of a parameter value and their numeric values.

mal:item.comment: The parameter has a timeout associated which has expired.
The parameter raw value cannot be obtained, or calculated for synthetic parameters.
The validity expression has evaluated to TRUE or there is no validity defined, but the conversion of the parameter value has failed (for example an unexpected value for a discrete conversion).
The validity expression has been evaluated to FALSE and therefore the current value cannot be verified.
The validity expression has been evaluated to FALSE.

mal:composite.name: ParameterDefinition
mal:composite.comment: The definition of a parameter, including name, type, reporting interval, validity expression, and optional conversion. For onboard parameters, the report interval should be a multiple of the minimum sampling interval of that parameter.

mal:field.name: name
mal:field.comment: The name of the parameter. Shall not be empty or the wildcard value.

mal:field.name: description
mal:field.comment: The description of the parameter. May be empty.

mal:field.name: rawType
mal:field.comment: The attribute short form part of the raw type of the parameter, e.g., for a MAL::String parameter this is 15.

mal:field.name: rawUnit
mal:field.comment: The unit for the raw value. If NULL then raw type has no unit.

mal:field.name: generationEnabled
mal:field.comment: Controls whether reports for this parameter are to be generated.

mal:field.name: reportInterval
mal:field.comment: Periodic report interval. No periodic reports to be generated if this is set to '0'.

mal:field.name: validityExpression
mal:field.comment: Expression that determines this parameter's validity state. Can be NULL if no validity check is required or validity is calculated by implementation-specific mechanisms.

mal:field.name: conversion
mal:field.comment: If present then parameter has a converted type.

mal:composite.name: ParameterValue
mal:composite.comment: A specific value of a parameter, including its validity state, raw value, and converted value. The type of the value shall match that specified in the parameter definition.

mal:field.name: validityState
mal:field.comment: The validity state for the parameter value. If the parameter is valid, this shall be set to '0'.

mal:field.name: rawValue
mal:field.comment: The parameter raw value. The value of NULL is a valid value and carries no special significance in the parameter service.

mal:field.name: convertedValue
mal:field.comment: The parameter converted value.

mal:composite.name: ParameterConversion
mal:composite.comment: The conversion configuration for a parameter, specifying the converted type, unit, and the ordered list of conditional conversions to apply.

mal:field.name: convertedType
mal:field.comment: The attribute short form part of the converted type of the parameter, e.g., for a MAL::String parameter this is 15.

mal:field.name: convertedUnit
mal:field.comment: The converted parameter unit. If NULL then converted type has no unit.

mal:field.name: conditionalConversions
mal:field.comment: The conversions to be applied. Only the first TRUE conversion should be applied.

mal:composite.name: ParameterRawValue
mal:composite.comment: A new raw value for a specific parameter, identified by its ParameterDefinition id.

mal:field.name: parameterId
mal:field.comment: The id of the parameter.

mal:field.name: rawValue
mal:field.comment: The parameter raw value. The value of NULL is a valid value and carries no special significance in the parameter service.

mal:composite.name: ParameterValueDetails
mal:composite.comment: A time-stamped value of a parameter, including the ParameterDefinition id and the ParameterValue. The type of the value shall match that specified in the parameter definition.

mal:field.name: defId
mal:field.comment: The id of the Parameter Definition.

mal:field.name: timestamp
mal:field.comment: The timestamp of the value.

mal:field.name: value
mal:field.comment: The parameter value.

mal:composite.name: AlertDefinition
mal:composite.comment: The AlertDefinition provides the definition of an alert including any argument definitions.

mal:field.name: name
mal:field.comment: The alert name. Shall not be empty or the wildcard value.

mal:field.name: description
mal:field.comment: The description of the alert.

mal:field.name: severity
mal:field.comment: Severity of the alert.

mal:field.name: generationEnabled
mal:field.comment: Controls whether instances of this alert are to be generated.

mal:field.name: arguments
mal:field.comment: The list of argument definitions.

mal:composite.name: AlertEvent
mal:composite.comment: The details of an instance of an alert, including the argument values associated with the event.

mal:field.name: argumentValues
mal:field.comment: List containing the values of the arguments. The ordering of the list matches that of the definition. If a value for a particular entry is not being supplied, then its position is filled with a NULL value. If no arguments are defined, then the complete list is replaced with a NULL.

mal:field.name: argumentIds
mal:field.comment: Optional list of argument definition identifiers. Allows the consumer to verify that the correct arguments are being supplied. The ordering of the list matches that of the argument list of the alert definition.

mal:item.comment: General aggregation.
Diagnostic aggregation.
Threshold value is a percentage.
Threshold value is a delta.

mal:enumeration.name: GenerationMode
mal:enumeration.comment: The reasons for which an aggregation report may be generated.

mal:item.comment: The aggregation value was generated because of an ad-hoc implementation dependent reason.
The aggregation value was generated because of a periodic report.
The item is filtered but it exceeded its timeout value.

mal:composite.name: AggregationDefinition
mal:composite.comment: The definition of an aggregation, including its name, reporting interval, filter settings, and the ordered list of parameter sets.

mal:field.name: name
mal:field.comment: The name of the aggregation. Shall not be empty or the wildcard value.

mal:field.name: description
mal:field.comment: The description of the parameter. May be empty.

mal:field.name: category
mal:field.comment: The category of the aggregation.

mal:field.name: reportInterval
mal:field.comment: The interval between periodic reports on this aggregation. If this aggregation is not periodic, this field shall be '0'.

mal:field.name: sendUnchanged
mal:field.comment: If TRUE reports will include all values regardless of whether changed, if FALSE values unchanged from previous report are replaced with a NULL.

mal:field.name: sendDefinitions
mal:field.comment: If TRUE reports will include the ParameterDefinition id in the AggregationParameterValue, if FALSE it will be set to NULL.

mal:field.name: filterEnabled
mal:field.comment: Controls whether reports for this aggregation are to be filtered.

mal:field.name: filteredTimeout
mal:field.comment: The maximum duration between filtered reports. If this value is exceeded, then a report is sent regardless of filtered thresholds. Ignored if not filtered.

mal:field.name: generationEnabled
mal:field.comment: Controls whether reports for this aggregation are to be generated.

mal:field.name: parameterSets
mal:field.comment: List containing the parameter sets which define the aggregation.

mal:composite.name: AggregationParameterSet
mal:composite.comment: A set of parameters within an aggregation definition, including the sample interval and an optional filter threshold.

mal:field.name: domain
mal:field.comment: The domain of the parameters being referenced in this set of parameters, NULL if the same domain as the aggregation.

mal:field.name: parameters
mal:field.comment: The list of ids of the ParameterDefinition objects being included in the aggregation.

mal:field.name: sampleInterval
mal:field.comment: The interval between samples of the parameters in the set. If '0' then just a single sample of the parameters is required per aggregation report.

mal:field.name: reportFilter
mal:field.comment: The filter to apply for filtered reports when applied. NULL if no filter required or this set contains more than one parameter.

mal:composite.name: AggregationValue
mal:composite.comment: The values for one or more parameter sets in an aggregation. The value sets shall be in the same order as defined in the matching AggregationDefinition.

mal:field.name: generationMode
mal:field.comment: Reason for the aggregation being generated.

mal:field.name: filtered
mal:field.comment: If a filter is enabled when the aggregation value is generated then this value shall be set to TRUE, else FALSE.

mal:field.name: parameterSetValues
mal:field.comment: The sets of values of the aggregation. The sets shall be in the same order as defined in the aggregation definition.

mal:composite.name: AggregationSetValue
mal:composite.comment: The values for one parameter set in an aggregation report, including optional timing information. If the sendUnchanged field in the AggregationDefinition is FALSE, parameter values unchanged since the previous report are replaced by NULL. The parameter values shall be in the same order as defined in the matching AggregationDefinition.

mal:field.name: deltaTime
mal:field.comment: Optional delta time, from the timestamp of the aggregation for the first parameter set of the aggregation or the last value of the previous parameter set otherwise, for the first parameter sample of this set. If NULL, then the first sample time is the same as the aggregation timestamp for the first parameter set of the aggregation or the last value of the previous parameter set otherwise.

mal:field.name: intervalTime
mal:field.comment: Optional delta time between samples in this set. If NULL, then all samples in this set are given the same time. This is usually driven by the sampleInterval in the aggregation set definition.

mal:field.name: values
mal:field.comment: List containing values of the parameters which are part of the aggregation. The ordering of the list entries shall match that of the definition of the aggregation. If there are more values than contained in the definition then it is assumed that the parameters cycle as a complete parameter set.

mal:composite.name: AggregationParameterValue
mal:composite.comment: A single parameter value within an aggregation, paired with its ParameterDefinition instance identifier.

mal:field.name: value
mal:field.comment: The parameter value.

mal:field.name: paramDefInstId
mal:field.comment: The id of the ParameterDefinition. NULL if sendDefinitions in the AggregationDefinition is FALSE.

mal:composite.name: ThresholdFilter
mal:composite.comment: The threshold filter for a parameter within an aggregation, specifying the type and value of the change threshold.

mal:field.name: thresholdType
mal:field.comment: The type of filter to apply for filtered periodic reports when filters are applied.

mal:field.name: thresholdValue
mal:field.comment: Threshold value to apply.

mal:field.name: useConverted
mal:field.comment: If true, and the relevant Parameter has a conversion, then use the converted value for the threshold comparison, otherwise use the raw value.

mal:composite.name: AggregationValueDetails
mal:composite.comment: A time-stamped value of an aggregation, including the AggregationDefinition id and the AggregationValue.

mal:field.name: defId
mal:field.comment: The AggregationDefinition id.

mal:field.name: timestamp
mal:field.comment: The timestamp of the value. Use for the calculation of the individual parameter value timestamps.

mal:field.name: value
mal:field.comment: The aggregation value.

mal:composite.name: DiscreteConversion
mal:composite.comment: A bidirectional conversion between raw and converted values defined by a discrete set of value pairs. The first element of each pair is the raw value and the second is the converted value. Both sets of values shall be unique.

mal:field.name: mapping
mal:field.comment: Defines a mapping between raw and converted values as a discrete set of points. The first entry in the pair is the raw value, and the second entry is the converted value.

mal:composite.name: LineConversion
mal:composite.comment: A bi-directional conversion between raw and converted values defined by a series of interpolation points. The extrapolate field indicates whether values can also be linearly extrapolated beyond the initial and final points.

mal:field.name: extrapolate
mal:field.comment: Indicates whether or not values can be extrapolated beyond the start and the end of the points.

mal:field.name: points
mal:field.comment: Defines the bi-directional conversion. The first attribute of the point is a raw value, and the second attribute is the converted value.

mal:composite.name: PolyConversion
mal:composite.comment: A forward-only (raw to converted) polynomial conversion defined by a series of coefficient points.

mal:field.name: points
mal:field.comment: The first attribute of a point is a MAL::Integer, being the degree of the polynomial; the second attribute is either a MAL::Float or a MAL::Double, being the coefficient of the term.

mal:composite.name: RangeConversion
mal:composite.comment: A one-way conversion from a continuous raw range to a discrete converted value. Each range is defined as from a point up to, but not including, the next point.

mal:field.name: points
mal:field.comment: The first attribute in each pair is the raw range, and the second attribute is the converted value.
